This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of the ascending clock mechanism. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a price exceeding my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $34, I will bid exactly that amount to ensure optimal outcomes in this one-shot round.

Since the winning price equals the second-highest bid (not my own), this functions like a second-price auction. Bidding my true value ($45) is the dominant strategy: if I win, I pay less than my value (profitable), and I never overpay since the price is capped by the second-highest bid. Bidding above or below my value only risks either winning at a loss or missing profitable wins.
